BlackThriveSS: path to CRAN

Source: CRAN-READINESS.md

Working version: 0.0.3.9000 (development). Review date: 22 October 2026. Scope: two immutable data releases (the original 2025 force_disparity dataset and a six-dataset catalogue from the same dashboard snapshot), the force ranking chart for any year and group, saved views, and the URL round trip with the dashboard website, plus, since 0.0.3: robustness analysis (btg_sensitivity(), btg_rank_stability(), btg_plot_sensitivity()), btg_robustness_summary()), trends and change (btg_plot_trend(), btg_change(), btg_plot_change()), a live-source check (btg_source_status(), the package’s only network use, which fails quietly and whose network test runs only when BLACKTHRIVESS_NETWORK_TESTS=true), profiles and HTML briefings (btg_profile(), btg_report()), exports and the glossary, schema 3 saved views, two further vignettes and a pkgdown configuration. The dashboard button is deferred. No CRAN submission or hosted release is created by this work.

Development checks since 0.0.3

  • Ubuntu 24.04 / R 4.6.1 (current release), on the development tree before these additions: R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual with remote incoming checks disabled completed with 0 errors, 0 warnings and 1 note, the note being the development version number (0.0.3.9000). An initial run also warned that the container could not set the en_US.UTF-8 locale, which is an environment matter resolved by generating the locale.
  • The same check on the development tree with the additions is recorded in artifacts/check-summary.json when dev/check-release.R is next run; see the commit message for the result at the time of the change.
  • Help pages are generated with roxygen2 8.1.1, which replaces the RoxygenNote field with Config/roxygen2/version and adds the repository links and author list to the package help page. Regenerating with an older roxygen2 will flip the field back; use 8.1 or later.
  • Known inaccuracy in the catalogue release: national_month_ethnicity and hit_rate_ethnicity_year list an Unknown group that has no rows in the bundled tables. A future catalogue build should drop it from groups; the data dictionary records it meanwhile.

Verified local results

The 0.0.3 source archive has SHA-256 4864d2a236b6f823e45a5f48db1bc0556bd490c9bd2eecbc902157f2e59df9ef (855 KB, of which about 0.8 MB is compressed data). The installation bundle contains this same archive.

  • Fresh-library installation passed, including a library path containing spaces. Existing dependency installations were reused; downloading dependencies onto a wholly fresh machine remains untested. A corrupted archive was rejected.
  • The quickstart, installed HTML tutorial, package citation, the validation audit of every bundled dataset and exact saved-view replay passed without a dashboard session.
  • All 210 packaged test assertions passed, with no failures, warnings or skips.
  • Dashboard parity, from dev/verify-dashboard.R against the dashboard’s own calculation functions and source-file hashes:
    • force_disparity: twelve fields across 42 rows, all 40 eligible ratios and three ordering modes matched; largest absolute numeric difference about 4.8e-13.
    • force_ethnicity_year: 36 year-and-group tables (2018 to 2026, four groups), 1,500 rows and 1,125 eligible ratios matched on twelve fields; largest absolute difference about 4.2e-10, from storing derived doubles to twelve significant figures. Where the dashboard divides by a zero White count and shows Inf, the package withholds the ratio as NA; both sides treat the cell as ineligible (West Midlands, 2018 to 2020, Asian and Other).
    • The 2025 Black rows of the catalogue equal the original release; the build script asserts this and a packaged test re-asserts it.
  • R CMD check --as-cran on Windows 11 / R 4.5.2 on this archive: see artifacts/check-summary.json and the section below. Remote incoming checks were explicitly disabled, as for 0.0.2, after the default attempt timed out retrieving CRAN’s package index. The 0.0.2 logs are retained under artifacts/checks/0.0.2 and artifacts/checks/0.0.2-local.

Machine-readable evidence is in artifacts/check-summary.json, artifacts/installation-test.json and artifacts/dashboard-parity.json. Run Rscript --vanilla dev/check-release.R with normal connectivity for the remote checks. --local-incoming is an explicit local fallback, not a substitute for the remaining pre-submission checks.

Local package check

R CMD check --as-cran on Windows 11 / R 4.5.2 on the 0.0.3 archive completed with 0 errors, 0 warnings and 1 note, with _R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_REMOTE_=false explicitly set. The note was unable to verify current time, an online time-check limitation that 0.0.2 also produced. Examples (12 s), tests (90 s), vignette rebuilding (15 s) and the PDF and HTML manuals passed. The full log is artifacts/checks/0.0.3-local/BlackThriveSS.Rcheck/00check.log, and artifacts/check-summary.json records the archive SHA-256, R version, errors, warnings and notes.

The first run of dev/check-release.R on this archive reached DONE but its R process was stopped by the script’s own ten-minute rcmdcheck timeout before it wrote the summary; the timeout is now 40 minutes. The check takes about twelve minutes on this workstation because the test suite replays every dataset through its checksum.

Release gates

Gate Evidence or next action
Source installation install.R and the installation ZIP resolve required dependencies, validate archive checksums and target a writable library. Record the fresh-session installation result.
User documentation Executed vignettes: getting started (catalogue, chart, URL round trip, validation, troubleshooting), robustness (bounds, rank intervals, change, export) and briefing (profiles, charts, the HTML briefing); function help; data dictionary with catalogue and derived-table sections; glossary; package and data citations. The briefing test and example skip without rmarkdown and Pandoc.
Data integrity Payload SHA-256 checks on every file, gzip payloads included, plus btg_validate() on every dataset: keys, whole counts, ethnicity accounting, coverage reconciliation and the documented calculations. Tests include deliberate corruption.
Mathematical correctness Hand-calculated count/exposure fixtures, zero/missing-count cases, denominator exclusions and eligibility thresholds, shared by the generic group calculation. Allocation bounds, rank bounds and change intervals are checked against independent hand calculations on transcribed Metropolitan Police counts; rank intervals are checked for reproducibility, bracketing and the identity that top-n probabilities sum to n.
Dashboard parity dev/verify-dashboard.R checks source hashes, the original 42-row table and three orderings, and all 36 year-and-group tables of the catalogue against the dashboard’s own functions.
URL round trip Tests cover both link forms the dashboard reads, all three orderings through the state form, legacy links with force labels, the dashboard’s default year and group, and explicit failures for other pages, the expanded definition, unknown years and groups, and malformed state. The live base address is configurable and has not been fetched from this package.
Historical replay The 2025 release and schema 1 views are unchanged and replay; schema 2 views carry year, group and highlight for both force ranking charts; schema 3 views carry a dataset selection and chart settings for trend and change charts, and settings are never evaluated.
Local package check Run dev/check-release.R. Results and archive SHA-256 are in artifacts/check-summary.json; all notes require review.
Current R and other systems Passed on GitHub Actions, 22 October 2026 (run 39811985340 on commit 3a7b890, the 0.0.3 source plus the URL/BugReports fields and a workflow fix): Windows release, macOS release, Ubuntu release, devel, oldrel-1 and R 4.1 all completed R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual with status OK and no notes, with the workflow set to fail on any warning. Re-run on the exact archive intended for submission.
Source-data review Reconfirm Police.uk and ONS attributions, population construction and disclosure scope for the council table. No restricted survey records are bundled. Statistical review should distinguish faithful reproduction from sound inference.
Ownership and support Maintainer contact and Black Thrive ownership are carried from the existing project metadata. Confirm final authorship, rights, support responsibility and email availability before public submission.
Public distribution The repository is https://github.com/BlackThrive/BlackThriveSS (private at creation; release 0.0.3 tagged v0.0.3), and DESCRIPTION carries matching URL and BugReports fields from 0.0.3.9000. Decide the visibility and release location, and preserve supported historical releases.
Name and final scope Check name availability immediately before submission; this document does not reserve the name. Keep the scope useful and adequately documented.

Package checks and submission

CRAN’s submission checklist asks for R CMD check --as-cran using current R-devel. It also identifies Win-builder and R-hub as supplementary services. Our multi-platform matrix is a project validation choice, not a claim that CRAN requires every matrix cell. CRAN submission checklist

The workstation has R 4.5.2; a clean result there does not establish current R-release/devel compatibility. Verify the actual release version when running external checks. Writing R Extensions

Keep package code and bundled data rights explicit; maintain examples that work without network access or writes outside temporary files. Review current policies again before submitting. CRAN acceptance also involves human review and ongoing maintenance. CRAN policies

After technical and ownership gates pass, freeze an intended submission archive, record its SHA-256, and complete cran-comments.md with actual environments and explanations of notes. Submit that archive through CRAN and complete the maintainer-email confirmation. Do not describe a submission as acceptance.

Exact artifact discipline

The build script produces artifacts/BlackThriveSS_0.0.3.tar.gz, artifacts/release/release.dcf, and the installation ZIP. Check the same source archive that will be distributed. If any included source, documentation or data changes, rebuild and re-check; do not carry forward an earlier pass. Earlier archives (0.0.1, 0.0.2) and their check directories are kept as history and are not the distributed build.

The data releases are dashboard-2026-07-2025-99a88b69f2d6 and dashboard-2026-07-catalogue-bacf49c2a48d, both from the same dashboard build of the July 2026 source month. A release directory is never overwritten; a changed source or method produces a new release identifier. Updating the package’s installation or help does not change a data release. Runtime users receive the aggregate snapshots with the package, so a hosted API is not a prerequisite for this first release.

External services

The CI workflow is based on the official r-lib/actions example and runs on every push to main of BlackThrive/BlackThriveSS. The first two runs failed before checking anything because the error-on input was passed unquoted and evaluated as an R symbol; the input is now '"warning"' as in the upstream example, and the matrix passes (see the release gates).

Win-builder sends results to the maintainer address and is a separate upload. Record any such result before claiming it passed. Win-builder

The dashboard link functions build and parse URL strings only. The default base address is the dashboard’s published share link; confirm it resolves before advertising the round trip, and set BlackThriveSS.dashboard_url for any other deployment.
